paragraphs: This paper studies how to make many statistical testing decisions when the underlying signals are sparse. Its central question is whether a relatively simple Bayesian model can attain the best achievable long-run decision quality. The authors approach this through relative belief ratios, which measure evidence by comparing prior and posterior beliefs.

The result applies within a specified framework: a two-groups model, additive zero-one loss, and a Bayesian asymptotic decision setting. Under these conditions, certain relative belief testing rules constructed from a light-tailed normal prior with one hyperparameter reach the same asymptotic Bayes risk as an oracle benchmark. That benchmark represents the minimum risk achievable in the framework.

The significance is that this optimality does not require the elaborate heavy-tailed shrinkage priors used by many existing Bayesian testing procedures. Comparing beliefs before and after observing data provides another route to oracle performance. The conclusion concerns asymptotic risk under the stated setup, rather than a guarantee of optimal decisions for every finite dataset.
icml-2026-an-evidential-route-to-asympto.tldr: Under a specified sparse-testing framework, simple relative belief rules achieve the same asymptotic Bayes risk as an oracle.

paragraphs: Generating several reasoning attempts helps only if a system can choose a good one. Confidence derived from output scores can become disconnected from correctness, while selecting the most common answer requires multiple samples and can be brittle. This paper investigates whether changes inside the model offer another useful selection signal.

The proposed Latent Velocity Entropy, or LVE, measures how concentrated internal representation updates are over the course of inference. It requires no training. Rather than judging an answer solely through output confidence or agreement with other answers, it characterizes the dynamics of the computation that produced it.

Across four reasoning benchmarks, LVE remains informative in cases where confidence baselines fail. Benefits are clearest on mathematically intensive reasoning and smaller on knowledge-heavy GPQA. On MATH500, LogNorm-LVE achieves 92.2% Pass@1 with ten candidates and nearly matches ten-sample majority voting using three samples. Cross-model and length-controlled analyses indicate that sequence length alone does not explain the signal, while confirming that its usefulness depends on the task.
icml-2026-beyond-logits-metastable-laten.tldr: A training-free measure of internal representation dynamics helps select reasoning answers with fewer samples, especially on mathematical tasks.

paragraphs: Clustering single-cell RNA sequencing data groups cells with similar gene expression patterns. Transformer attention can help separate these groups by emphasizing relationships among similar cells. However, treating every cell as a token makes existing approaches expensive: their computation and memory requirements grow quadratically with the number of cells.

BGFormer introduces learnable anchor tokens that act as shared reference points for the dataset. Its bipartite attention mechanism learns relationships between cells and these anchors. This changes the structure of the comparison problem: cells relate to a common set of references, and the learned representation brings cells of the same class closer together.

The resulting model has computational complexity that grows linearly with cell count, addressing the scaling obstacle identified in the paper. Experiments on multiple large single-cell datasets support both its clustering effectiveness and scalability. The contribution combines a representation-learning mechanism with a computational redesign, allowing attention to help organize cell populations without retaining the quadratic computational growth of the described cell-token approaches.
icml-2026-bipartite-graph-attention-base.tldr: BGFormer uses shared learnable anchors to cluster single-cell data with computation that scales linearly with cell count.

paragraphs: Estimating how different treatments affect an individual becomes harder as the number and complexity of treatment options increase. This paper addresses two obstacles: choosing the weight used to balance treatment representations and keeping that balancing process computationally manageable. Both affect whether a method can handle a large intervention space.

The authors derive a generalization bound for multiple treatments and use it to construct a theoretical estimator for the balancing weight. This replaces expensive heuristic tuning. They compare pairwise balancing, one-versus-all balancing, and treatment aggregation. One-versus-all is more precise in low-dimensional settings, while treatment aggregation is reported to maintain accuracy with constant-order scalability as the treatment space grows.

The framework also extends to Multi-Treatment CausalEGM, a generative architecture designed to preserve Wasserstein geodesic structure in the treatment manifold. This retains a particular geometric relationship among treatments during representation learning. Experiments on semi-synthetic and image datasets report improvements over traditional models in estimation accuracy and efficiency, especially for large intervention scenarios. The results make the choice of balancing strategy consequential to both precision and scaling.
icml-2026-causal-representation-learning.tldr: A theoretically selected balancing weight and treatment aggregation improve the accuracy and scalability of multi-treatment effect estimation.

paragraphs: A link recommendation system helps shape the network it later learns from: showing a potential connection changes whether that connection forms. Consequently, observed outcomes can give a misleading picture of fairness, and fairness can shift when the recommendation policy changes. COPF addresses this feedback problem at the recommendation decision layer.

The framework defines group opportunity gaps using counterfactual comparisons between showing and withholding candidate links. It introduces explicit exploration and records each candidate's probability of being shown so those comparisons can be estimated. Graph-aware doubly robust estimators support an auditor that checks residual outcome indistinguishability, alongside a controller that adjusts decisions.

A transfer theorem connects these residual checks to bounds on counterfactual group gaps under temporal mixing and bounded local interference. These assumptions qualify the theoretical guarantee. Experiments on two TGB streams and a controlled synthetic stream find that COPF reduces the worst disparity spikes with a modest effect on ranking utility. The contribution therefore combines a measurable fairness target, conditions supporting its interpretation, and an online mechanism for controlling it.
icml-2026-copf-an-online-framework-for-d.tldr: COPF monitors and controls counterfactual fairness in evolving link recommendations, reducing disparity spikes with modest ranking impact in experiments.

paragraphs: Language model pretraining requires choosing how much data to draw from different sources. That choice influences the balance between broad competence and difficult capabilities such as mathematics and coding. Testing many mixtures directly is expensive, while results from very small proxy models may not reliably guide larger training runs.

DeMix changes how candidate mixtures are evaluated. It first trains component models on candidate datasets at scale, then combines those models with different weights to produce proxies for different data ratios. Once the components exist, additional mixture candidates do not require separate proxy training runs. This separates the cost of training components from the number of mixtures explored.

The experiments report better benchmark performance and lower search cost when identifying an optimal mixture through this process. The benefit is a wider search supported by proxies built from models trained at scale; evaluating those proxies still remains part of the search. The authors also release DeMix Corpora, a 22-trillion-token collection of high-quality pretraining data with validated mixtures, supporting further research into data composition.
icml-2026-decouple-searching-from-traini.tldr: DeMix searches pretraining data mixtures through weighted model merging, avoiding a new proxy training run for each candidate.

paragraphs: Coordinating multiple learning agents requires policies expressive enough to represent different useful actions. Diffusion models offer that flexibility, but their action likelihoods are difficult to compute. This creates a problem for online reinforcement learning methods that use entropy to encourage exploration and coordinate agents' behavior.

OMAD is an online, off-policy framework that uses diffusion policies for multiple agents. Its central change is a relaxed objective that maximizes scaled joint entropy without requiring tractable policy likelihoods. During centralized training, a joint distributional value function guides the decentralized policies using computable entropy-augmented targets. The policies are updated together to support stable coordination.

This design follows centralized training with decentralized execution: learning can use joint information while execution remains distributed across agents. Evaluations on ten tasks from MPE and MAMuJoCo report state-of-the-art performance and improvements of 2.5 to 5 times in sample efficiency. These findings support the framework's ability to make expressive diffusion policies practical for the evaluated online coordination problems, where learning efficiently from interaction is central.
icml-2026-diffusing-to-coordinate-effici.tldr: OMAD enables entropy-guided online learning with decentralized diffusion policies, reporting 2.5–5 times better sample efficiency across ten coordination tasks.

paragraphs: Membership inference attempts to determine whether a particular image was used to train a model. For diffusion models, many attacks use image prediction behavior to derive a membership score. This paper organizes those attacks into a common framework and identifies a frequency-related source of errors in their decisions.

The authors find that diffusion models' difficulty processing high-frequency information can distort membership scores. Training images containing more high-frequency content can be mistaken for unseen images, while unseen images with less of that content can be mistaken for training examples. Their theoretical analysis also shows that this deficiency reduces membership advantage, weakening the distinction the attacks are meant to detect.

The proposed remedy is a high-frequency filtering module that can be added to attacks within the unified framework. It aims to reduce the influence of the identified deficiency and is reported to add no time cost. Experiments across different datasets and models show substantial improvements to baseline attacks. The finding matters because image content can confound a privacy test unless the scoring process accounts for this model behavior.
icml-2026-enhancing-membership-inference.tldr: A high-frequency filter improves diffusion-model membership inference by reducing a content-related bias in existing attack scores.

paragraphs: Medical image screening models can produce predictions without clearly connecting them to relevant prior cases or showing where abnormalities are supported. EviScreen addresses both issues by making regional evidence from historical cases part of the prediction process. Its aim is to improve screening performance while giving users more interpretable evidence.

The framework retrieves region-level information from two knowledge banks. An evidence-aware reasoning module then combines the current case with that historical evidence to make its prediction. This creates a retrospective explanation: a prediction can be understood through the retrieved regions that informed it. The method also derives abnormality maps through contrastive retrieval, providing a localization mechanism within its evidential approach.

On the authors' benchmarks for real-world disease screening, EviScreen achieves superior performance, including higher specificity at clinically relevant recall. In practical terms, that result means better rejection of negative cases while retaining the reported level of disease detection. The two forms of interpretability serve complementary purposes: historical regions expose supporting comparisons, while abnormality maps indicate where relevant evidence appears in the image.
icml-2026-evidential-reasoning-advances-.tldr: EviScreen uses regional evidence from historical cases to improve screening specificity and make predictions and abnormality locations more interpretable.

paragraphs: Editing a latent diffusion model's internal representation can produce abrupt changes in image meaning, even when the intended edit is small. This paper examines that brittleness through the geometry of the generative mapping. It asks how the local structure of latent space relates to useful image detail and unstable semantic changes.

The authors use a Riemannian framework based on the generative Jacobian, which describes local sensitivity of generated output to latent changes. They separate local scaling, interpreted as capacity, from local complexity, interpreted as curvature. In normal generation, curvature functionally represents image detail. In out-of-distribution generation, the study finds that extreme curvature can instead concentrate around unstable semantic boundaries.

The authors call this mismatch geometric decoupling: geometric complexity becomes disconnected from perceptible detail. They identify the resulting geometric hotspots as the structural source of instability and use them to motivate an intrinsic diagnostic metric for generative reliability. The contribution explains why high local complexity can correspond to useful detail in one setting and brittle editing behavior in another.
icml-2026-geometric-decoupling-diagnosin.tldr: A geometric analysis links latent diffusion instability to extreme curvature concentrated at semantic boundaries rather than visible image detail.

paragraphs: Multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion models commonly expect a fixed number of spectral bands and a fixed spatial scale. Those expectations make it difficult to reuse one model across sensors with different characteristics. SSA addresses both sources of rigidity within a single framework for combining these types of imagery.

Its Matryoshka Kernel operator supports varying counts of ordered spectral bands within a supported range. Separately, an implicit neural representation describes the hyperspectral signal as a continuous function. That continuous representation allows reconstruction to be queried at arbitrary spatial resolutions. Together, the two mechanisms let one model accommodate differences in spectral input and requested output scale.

The authors report that a single jointly trained model achieves state-of-the-art performance and generalizes to spatial scales it did not encounter during training. Transfer to unseen sensors is also demonstrated with a few adaptation steps. These qualifications matter: spectral flexibility remains within the operator's supported range, and the reported sensor transfer involves adaptation. The results support broader reuse of a fusion model across heterogeneous imaging setups.
icml-2026-hyperspectral-image-fusion-wit.tldr: SSA combines flexible spectral-band processing with continuous spatial reconstruction to support one fusion model across scales and adaptable sensor settings.

paragraphs: A robot policy can appear to follow language while actually relying on visual cues alone. This paper traces that failure to goal-driven data collection: when the image already makes the instruction predictable, language can contribute no additional information about the action. The authors name this training pathology Information Collapse.

LangForce introduces learnable latent action queries and two branches. One estimates an action distribution from vision alone, while the other estimates actions conditioned on both vision and language. A conditional pointwise mutual information objective compares these distributions, rewarding actions that are specifically supported by the instruction and penalizing reliance on the visual shortcut.

This construction makes language's contribution explicit in the training objective. It addresses the difficulty of generalizing to new commands and complex combinations of tasks when visual context alone is insufficient to express the requested behavior. Across three benchmarks, the authors report substantial gains, including an 11.3% improvement on out-of-distribution SimplerEnv. The results support improved grounding of instructions in robot actions under the evaluated conditions.
icml-2026-langforce-bayesian-decompositi.tldr: LangForce compares vision-only and language-conditioned action predictions to train robot policies that use instructions more effectively.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models have expanded from language into multimodal understanding and generation. LaViDa-R1 investigates how to develop reasoning across those capabilities within one general-purpose model. The problem is broader than improving a single specialized task: the training framework must support diverse tasks involving both interpretation and generation.

The proposed post-training process combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning across multiple tasks. It also incorporates answer-forcing, tree search, and complementary likelihood estimation to improve training effectiveness and scalability. These techniques form part of a unified recipe, allowing the model's reasoning development to encompass several multimodal objectives together.

Experiments report strong performance across visual mathematical reasoning, grounding that requires substantial reasoning, and image editing. Those applications span understanding visual information, identifying relevant content, and producing requested changes. Their breadth supports the paper's claim that unified post-training can develop reasoning capabilities across different multimodal activities. The contribution is the integration of those activities into one diffusion-language-model training framework, extending beyond the task-specific reinforcement learning approach described in earlier work.
icml-2026-lavida-r1-advancing-reasoning-.tldr: LaViDa-R1 combines supervised fine-tuning and multi-task reinforcement learning to develop reasoning across multimodal understanding and generation.

paragraphs: An agent following spoken or written directions needs spatial context beyond its current view. Many navigation systems supply that context through manually designed maps built separately from the navigation policy. MapDream instead learns a map whose contents are shaped by what the agent needs to navigate successfully.

The framework generates bird's-eye-view maps autoregressively and learns map generation jointly with action prediction. Its compact, three-channel map retains navigation-critical affordances rather than attempting an exhaustive reconstruction of the environment. Supervised pretraining first establishes a reliable connection between mapping and control, giving the system a starting point for learning how its maps support actions.

Reinforcement fine-tuning then jointly optimizes the map and navigation policy end to end. This places map construction inside the learning process, so the representation can develop around navigation objectives. Experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE report state-of-the-art monocular performance. The results support the central proposal that a generated map can be useful because it preserves task-relevant spatial information, even when it is deliberately compact.
icml-2026-mapdream-task-driven-map-learn.tldr: MapDream jointly learns compact bird's-eye-view maps and navigation actions, reporting state-of-the-art monocular results on two navigation benchmarks.

paragraphs: An image can contain several compatible labels, but frozen vision-language models commonly score each label independently. Under distribution shift, strong concepts can suppress weaker ones and produce incoherent predictions. Bayesian Conditional Priors, or BCP, adds information about label relationships without updating the model's backbone.

For each image, BCP chooses a high-confidence anchor label and adjusts other label scores using priors conditioned on that anchor. Its Bayesian formulation treats zero-shot scores as approximate marginal posteriors and attributes shift errors mainly to a mismatched label prior under a fixed image-text likelihood. The closed-form adjustment promotes compatible labels and suppresses incompatible ones, with a pointwise mutual information interpretation.

BCP estimates the needed priors online from co-occurrence statistics in the unlabeled test stream. It uses no target annotations or gradients and adds negligible overhead beyond one forward pass. Across multi-label benchmarks, reported average mAP rises from 57.31 to 69.22 for RN50 and from 62.61 to 71.79 for ViT-B/16. These results support correcting label dependencies as an effective adaptation mechanism under the method's modeling assumptions.
icml-2026-multi-label-test-time-adaptati.tldr: BCP improves frozen vision-language models' multi-label predictions by learning label co-occurrence priors from unlabeled test data.

paragraphs: Incorrect training labels can damage a model because a sufficiently flexible network may learn to reproduce the mistakes. This paper detects potentially mislabeled images by observing how predictions evolve during training. Its key observation is that prediction entropy tends to decrease consistently for correctly labeled examples, while mislabeled examples retain relatively high entropy.

The proposed signed entropy integral, or SEI, summarizes both the amount of prediction uncertainty and its direction of change across training epochs. Tracking these two aspects preserves information about a sample's learning trajectory. The resulting statistic can be used with classification networks broadly, with particular effectiveness reported for CLIP-based architectures.

Experiments cover four medical imaging datasets spanning different modalities and pathologies, where diagnostic complexity makes labeling errors especially relevant. SEI achieves state-of-the-art identification performance in these evaluations while retaining computational efficiency and implementation simplicity. The finding suggests that the course of learning provides useful evidence about label reliability: persistent uncertainty and its evolution can help distinguish suspicious labels from examples the model learns more consistently.
icml-2026-on-revisiting-entropy-for-iden.tldr: SEI identifies mislabeled images by summarizing prediction uncertainty and its evolution throughout training.

paragraphs: Reasoning models can spend a long time working internally before showing anything useful to the user. If that work begins from a mistaken premise, the user has little opportunity to correct it early. This paper proposes interleaving internal reasoning with visible intermediate responses to create earlier opportunities for feedback.

The post-training recipe teaches the model to present an explicit, step-by-step plan before continuing its reasoning. The plan gives the user an early view of the intended approach while preserving room for further computation afterward. This creates a concrete interface for intervention: the model's direction becomes visible before it completes all of its reasoning.

Across mathematics, coding, text-to-SQL, and reading-comprehension benchmarks, the method improves pass@1 by roughly 6% on average and reduces time to the first response by more than 60% compared with think-then-answer baselines. The latency result concerns the first visible response, while the accuracy result concerns successful answers. Together, they show that earlier communication can coexist with stronger task performance in the reported evaluations.
icml-2026-plantain-plan-answer-interleav.tldr: Plan-first interleaved reasoning produces earlier visible responses while improving average pass@1 across several reasoning domains.

paragraphs: Language models normally receive position information based on a predetermined ordering. RePo argues that this rigid structure leaves attention layers responsible for discovering how the input's pieces relate to one another. That organizational burden can reduce the attention available for identifying the information most relevant to a task.

RePo introduces a differentiable module that assigns token positions according to contextual dependencies. Positions can therefore reflect relationships within the input instead of being limited to predefined indices. The authors apply this mechanism through continued pretraining of OLMo-2 models with one billion and seven billion parameters.

The resulting models improve consistently on tasks involving noisy context, structured data, and longer contexts, while remaining competitive on general short-context tasks. Analysis finds that relevant but distant information receives more attention and that the learned positions occupy a dense, nonlinear space. These observations support the proposed mechanism: changing positional structure can help the model organize context and direct attention toward useful relationships that ordinary sequence distance does not adequately express.
icml-2026-repo-language-models-with-cont.tldr: RePo learns context-dependent token positions to improve how language models use noisy, structured, and long inputs.

paragraphs: Video object-centric learning represents objects as slots and must keep those representations associated with the same objects across frames. Common approaches learn a dynamics model to predict future slots. This paper argues that these predictors act as costly approximations to a correspondence problem: determining which current object matches which earlier object.

Grounded Correspondence uses instance-discriminative features already present in modern self-supervised vision backbones. Slots begin from salient regions in the frozen backbone's features. Hungarian matching then establishes frame-to-frame associations between slot representations, replacing a learned temporal transition with deterministic bipartite matching.

The framework requires no learnable parameters for temporal modeling and achieves competitive results on MOVi-D, MOVi-E, and YouTube-VIS. The zero-parameter claim applies specifically to the temporal component; the approach still relies on the backbone's learned visual features. Its significance is that sufficiently informative object features can support temporal identity through direct matching, making a separate learned predictor unnecessary in the demonstrated framework. This reframes temporal consistency around correspondence rather than forecasting future representations.
icml-2026-rethinking-temporal-consistenc.tldr: Grounded Correspondence maintains video object identities through deterministic matching, achieving competitive results without learned temporal parameters.

paragraphs: Language-guided segmentation requires a system to identify the image or video regions described by a query. Some queries also depend on specialized or current knowledge. A multimodal model's fixed internal knowledge can therefore become a bottleneck even when the model has the reasoning ability needed to interpret the request.

Seg-ReSearch combines reasoning with external search, allowing the segmentation process to obtain information beyond the model's stored knowledge. Its training uses hierarchical rewards that combine initial guidance with progressive incentives. This design addresses the tension between providing too little feedback through final outcomes and imposing overly rigid supervision on every intermediate step.

The authors introduce OK-VOS, a video object segmentation benchmark whose queries explicitly require outside knowledge. Experiments on that benchmark and two existing reasoning segmentation benchmarks report substantial improvements over state-of-the-art approaches. The results support treating information acquisition as part of segmentation itself: the system can seek relevant knowledge while deciding which object or region a language query refers to, expanding the kinds of requests it can address.
icml-2026-seg-research-segmentation-with.tldr: Seg-ReSearch interleaves external search with reasoning to improve segmentation for queries requiring knowledge beyond a model's training.

paragraphs: Neural speech codecs turn audio into discrete tokens that speech language models can use. Quantization introduces errors that limit reconstructed audio quality. Increasing model size or changing the quantizer can address those errors, but the resulting token representation can become harder for a downstream language model to handle.

Self-guidance trains the decoder to align its internal features when processing quantized tokens and the corresponding original continuous embeddings. A lightweight feature-mapping loss encourages those internal representations to agree. The method adds minimal training overhead and requires no changes at inference time, making the decoder's training behavior the main point of intervention.

Applied to XCodec2, self-guidance improves all reported reconstruction metrics and achieves state-of-the-art low-bitrate performance. It also supports a fourfold reduction in codebook size without fidelity loss. Downstream text-to-speech experiments show significantly better language-model-based synthesis with the simpler token space. Statistical analyses and visualizations support improved internal alignment, while experiments across different inductive biases support the method's broader applicability. The results connect better codec reconstruction with easier downstream token modeling.
icml-2026-self-guidance-enhancing-neural.tldr: Aligning decoder features for continuous and quantized audio improves reconstruction and enables a fourfold smaller codebook without fidelity loss.

paragraphs: Direct Preference Optimization trains language models using preferred and dispreferred responses, making unreliable preference labels a problem. Some methods use differences in perplexity to judge label reliability. This paper finds that the signal depends strongly on the task: it correlates well with preference quality for factual prompts but weakly for creative prompts, where novelty matters.

Task-Aware Preference Calibration, or TAPC, learns how to interpret that signal for different prompt types. A task encoder represents the prompt, and task-specific slope and bias parameters map perplexity differences into confidence targets. Meta-learning on a small reference dataset teaches the system how much weight to give the signal for each task category.

Experiments with Llama-3-8B and Qwen2-7B show improvements over existing methods across multiple benchmarks. Gains are particularly large on creative and open-ended tasks, where uniform calibration performs poorly. The contribution is a way to account for the changing meaning of a reliability indicator: a useful clue for factual quality should receive a different interpretation when the task rewards novel responses.
icml-2026-task-aware-preference-calibrat.tldr: TAPC calibrates preference-label confidence by task type, improving DPO especially on creative and open-ended tasks.

paragraphs: Giving language models more inference-time computation can improve reasoning, but sequential generation creates delays. Parallel reasoning aims to reduce those delays, yet existing approaches can lose accuracy or require specialized inference systems. ThreadWeaver develops a training and execution framework intended to make parallel reasoning both accurate and broadly usable.

The framework has three components. A two-stage generator creates parallel reasoning trajectories for supervised fine-tuning. A trie-based rollout structure allows those trajectories to run on standard autoregressive inference engines. Reinforcement learning then explicitly balances reasoning accuracy with effective parallelization, making the ability to use parallel computation part of the model's training objective.

Built on Qwen3-8B, ThreadWeaver is evaluated on six difficult mathematics benchmarks. It reports 79.9% on AIME24 and a 71.9% average, matching the performance of comparably sized leading sequential reasoning models while achieving up to 1.53 times speedup in token latency. These findings establish an improved reported accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. The speedup is an upper reported result, and the empirical evidence concerns the evaluated mathematical reasoning tasks.
icml-2026-threadweaver-adaptive-threadin.tldr: ThreadWeaver trains adaptive parallel reasoning that matches comparable sequential models' math accuracy with up to 1.53 times faster token latency.

paragraphs: Transferring lighting from a reference photograph is difficult because the lighting is entangled with the objects and scene depicted. Structured effects such as beams and specular highlights make this particularly challenging. TransLight aims to transfer these effects with flexible control while preserving the target image's content.

Its Generative Decoupling stage uses two fine-tuned diffusion models to separate image content from illumination. The authors use this process to build a million-scale dataset of image, content, and light triplets. They then train IC-Light on those triplets, adding the reference lighting image as a conditioning signal for generation.

Separating the lighting provides a representation of the desired effect that can guide its application to another image. Experiments in portrait photography show transfer of geometrically structured illumination across diverse images, with more customized control than existing methods. The contribution connects data construction to controllable generation: the separated examples teach the model to use reference illumination, while the additional conditioning input supplies the particular effect requested at editing time.
icml-2026-translight-image-guided-custom.tldr: TransLight separates lighting from reference-image content to enable flexible transfer of structured illumination effects in portrait photography.

paragraphs: Drone autopilots depend on navigation and flight-control modules working together at appropriate times. When those modules run on separate hardware, the system has limited visibility across the full pipeline and fewer opportunities for joint scheduling. Flight performance also depends on interacting effects that accumulate over time, making scheduling difficult to capture with simple rules.

UAV² places navigation and flight control on one onboard computing platform and operating system. It models scheduling as a partially observable Markov decision process and uses reinforcement learning to choose schedules from runtime feedback. This gives the scheduler a way to learn from execution behavior while accounting for incomplete observation of the system.

Training and evaluation take place in a hardware-in-the-loop simulation environment. In those experiments, the learned policy consistently outperforms fixed-rate scheduling in flight robustness and tracking performance. The result supports coordinating computation across the integrated autopilot pipeline rather than assigning module rates independently. Its demonstrated benefit is tied to the reported simulation setup, where actual hardware participates in the evaluation.
icml-2026-uav-2-a-unified-and-adaptive-s.tldr: UAV² integrates autopilot modules and learns adaptive schedules that improve robustness and tracking over fixed-rate scheduling in hardware-in-the-loop simulation.
